item.title: A Proxy of Social Justice? A Co/Autoethnographic Account of Language Testing and Translation Training for Migrant Workers in Thailand
item.description: This article explores the possibilities and limits of advancing social justice through language-related support for migrant workers in Thailand. Using collaborative autoethnography, we reflect on our experiences in two university-led initiatives with Myanmar migrant workers: healthcare translator/interpreter training and Thai language proficiency testing, with ad hoc translation support. item.title: Robots at the Table: Unveiling Employee Experiences of Robot Integration in Malaysia’s Hospitality Industry
item.description: This study examines how frontline restaurant employees in Malaysia experience and interpret the integration of service robots within a labor-scarce hospitality sector characterized by reliance on a migrant workforce and high-touch service traditions. item.title: Thailand’s Sport Broadcasting Landscape: Policy, Progress, and Prospects
item.description: Over the past several decades, Thailand has undergone significant transformations in sport media policy, driven by shifts in national governance. The transition from conventional sport broadcasting to digital sport media has introduced several key challenges for Thai society. item.title: From Trauma to Legend: Ghost Narratives and Postwar Memory in Mỹ Lai
item.description: This article examines how contemporary ghost legends related to the Mỹ Lai Massacre (March 16, 1968) shape collective memory in postwar Vietnam. item.title: Sacred Ground, Contested Space: Deathscapes in the Aftermath of an Environmental Disaster in East Java, Indonesia
item.description: This study explores the sociocultural, economic, and symbolic significance of graveyards – conceptualized as deathscapes – among survivors of the Lapindo mudflow disaster in Sidoarjo, East Java. Drawing on ethnographic engagement and qualitative interviews, the research reveals how graveyards serve not only as burial sites but also as spaces of memory, resistance, and identity. item.title: Entering the Mind as a Way of Approaching God: Practicing Meditation and Being Muslim in Semarang, Indonesia
item.description: This article explores the ways in which Muslim meditation practitioners in Indonesia understand and utilize Buddhist meditative practice. Focusing on the narrative of one such practitioner, we draw out the little-known role that meditation plays in the everyday life of being Muslim. We pay special attention to how three meditation-related themes are entwined with the performance of the Islamic obligatory daily prayers to open up a space for contemplating and reconceiving a relationship with God

item.title: Digital Strike: Monetizing Online Engagement and Content for Myanmar’s Spring Revolution

item.title: Understanding Low Ecovillage Adoption in Southeast Asia: Insights from Malaysia Using Diffusion of Innovation Theory
item.description: The world is facing multiple intertwined crises, like environmental degradation and socioeconomic inequalities.
